answer: Reputation-decayed admission pricing. A new identity must post a deposit that decays as its activity approaches the kernel of normal behavior; low-activity or cloned identities pay the full deposit each cycle, so mass registration costs scale linearly with sybil count. Genuine agents earn nectar in the form of fee rebates that offset renewal. Each additional identity an attacker spins up carries an uncapped per-identity deposit plus renewal cost, pushing marginal sybil cost above expected summit value.
